1	# Protocol B (r3) — minimal, neutral scoping of candidate norm-provenance channels
2	
3	**Goal (from QUESTIONS.md):** decide, for a *bounded* list of locally checkable, read-only
4	channel types, whether any could be an **independent** record of *which norm was in force at
5	time t*. "Independent" = controlled by someone/something other than (a) the norm-maker,
6	(b) the executor of the work, (c) the ruling asserting its own effect. Existence/scoping only —
7	**no archaeology**, no evidence acquisition, **never a forced negative**.
8	
9	The research programme's own artefacts (`docs/knowledgeos/**`) are **never** candidates
10	(self-contamination) and are excluded by the classifier and from E.
11	
12	## 1. Candidate channels (exact patterns)
13	
14	Doc-like ext = `md,markdown,txt,rst,json,ya?ml,toml,csv,tsv`. Every token match below (K-NORMREG,
15	K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY) uses the leading boundary `(^|[/._-])` and the trailing token boundary `([._/-]|$)`
16	(BLK-2). A token can therefore start a path segment, or it can follow `.`, `_` or `-` inside a name
17	(e.g. `ADR-0007-Rulings.md`, `PROGRAM_STATUS.md`). It must end at `.`, `_`, `/`, `-` or the end of the path.
18	
19	| Id | What | Path pattern / source (case-insensitive) |
20	|----|------|-------------------------------------------|
21	| `K-CI` | CI definitions | `.github/workflows/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.circleci/**`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.drone.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.woodpecker*` |
22	| `K-HOOK` | repo-shipped git hooks | `.githooks/**`, `.husky/**`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.lefthook.yml` |
23	| `K-CODEOWNERS` | ownership / branch-protection hints in repo | path basename `CODEOWNERS` |
24	| `K-NORMREG` | norm register / rulings register / in-force record (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`) | doc-like ext and path matching the **register regex** `(^|[/._-])(rulings?|register|registry|decisions?|norm|inforce|authoriz(ation|ations)?)([._/-]|$)` |
25	| `K-STATUS` | the **remaining** status / progress / approval / sign-off records (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`); **disjoint** from `K-NORMREG` | doc-like ext, **not** `K-NORMREG`, path matching `(^|[/._-])`+token+`([._/-]|$)` for a token in {`program_status,status,ruling(s),register,registry,decision(s),adoption(s),approval(s),signoff(s),progress,inforce,norm`}, e.g. `docs/implementation/PROGRAM_STATUS.md` |
26	| `K-DEPLOY` | deployment / config **state** | path token (`(^|[/._-])`+token+`([._/-]|$)`) in {`deploy,deployment,release,environment,env,infra,terraform`} or ext `tfstate` |
27	| `K-SIG` | signed commits / tags | **presence** of `gpgsig` header / `-----BEGIN (PGP\|SSH) SIGNATURE-----`; keyring **not** consulted, signatures **not** verified |
28	| `K-LOCALHOOK` | local hooks (`LOCAL_ONLY`) | `.git/hooks/<standard-name>` present, or `core.hooksPath` set |
29	
30	**E-exclusion globs = classifier regex, by construction (BLK-2).** For each doc token t (the union
31	of the K-NORMREG and K-STATUS tokens, with `authoriz`, `authorization`, `authorizations` written out) and
32	each doc ext x, E excludes (`:(exclude,glob,icase)`):
33	- token at segment start: `**/$t.$x`, `**/$t[._-]*.$x`, `**/$t/**/*.$x`, `**/$t[._-]*/**/*.$x`;
34	- token after `.`/`_`/`-`: `**/*[._-]$t.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t[._-]*.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t/**/*.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t[._-]*/**/*.$x`.
35	
36	For each K-DEPLOY token t it excludes `**/$t`, `**/$t/**`, `**/$t[._-]*`, `**/$t[._-]*/**`, the same four
37	forms with `*[._-]` in front of t, and also `**/*.tfstate`.
38	
39	The glob set and the regex are **equivalent by construction**. Each glob form is exactly one case of
40	the regex:
41	- the leading boundary is either `^`/`/` (→ `**/`) or `.`/`_`/`-` (→ `**/*[._-]`);
42	- the trailing boundary is one of: the extension dot of the basename (→ `.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside the
43	  basename (→ `[._-]*.$x`); `/` (→ `/**/*.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside a directory segment (→ `[._-]*/**/*.$x`).
44	
45	For doc tokens, the path-end case `$` cannot occur: the path must end in `.$x`, and no token is a doc
46	extension. For K-DEPLOY, the path-end case is the bare `$t` form. The construction relies on these git
47	wildmatch semantics: `*` does not cross `/`; `**/` and `/**/` match zero or more directories; `icase`
48	is ASCII case folding, like awk `tolower` under `LC_ALL=C`. **No residual mismatch is known at the
49	pattern level.** The equivalence is argued, not executed. By design (§3), the globs are applied to
50	historic paths and the regex to tip paths.
51	
52	**Host-side channels — `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`** (host not authorized): `K-HOST-AUDIT`
53	(server audit logs), `K-HOST-BRANCHPROT` (branch-protection *enforcement*), `K-HOST-PR-APPROVALS`
54	(PR approvals), `K-CI-RUNS` (CI run history), `K-HOST-MEMBERS` (org/team membership).
55	
56	**The one tip set (B1, N5, N12).** Every history query (paths, W, commit counts, E, N_c, K-SIG)
57	runs over **one** tip file via `git log --stdin` / `git rev-list --stdin`. Tips = refs under
58	`refs/heads/**`, `refs/remotes/**`, `refs/tags/**` only (`refs/stash`, `refs/notes/**` excluded);
59	tags are peeled (`^{commit}`), and **only commit-type tips** are kept. The result does not depend
60	on the checked-out HEAD. Paths are read with `ls-tree -r -z` (N9).
61	
62	## 2. Deterministic answer rules
63	
64	Scope = the **tip set only**; completeness vs the host is never shown. `ND` =
65	`NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK`, `IND` = `INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE`. If a path channel
66	has **0** paths in the tip trees → Q1 = `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` (it may still exist in history
67	behind the tips) and Q2..Q8 = `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`; same label for `K-SIG` when no signature is
68	present in commits reachable from the tips or in tag objects at the tips; `K-LOCALHOOK` uses
69	`NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY`. Host rows are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` for all eight.
70	
71	- **Q1 exists** → `YES_IN_CAPTURE` | `YES_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`) | `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` | `NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY` | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
72	- **Q2 records** → by **type** only: `CONFIG_RULE` (K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-LOCALHOOK), `NORM_REGISTER_RECORD` (K-NORMREG), `STATUS_RECORD` (K-STATUS), `STATE_RECORD_BY_TYPE` (K-DEPLOY), `IDENTITY_ATTESTATION` (K-SIG); content not read.
73	- **Q3 controls** → `CONTROLLED_BY_WRITERS[n=…]` (count only) | for `K-SIG` `ND(keyring not consulted)` | `LOCAL_MACHINE` (`K-LOCALHOOK`).
74	- **Q4 timestamps independent** → `NO_CLIENT_SET` (git recording times are client-generated; a self-attested timestamp is **not** independence). Content timestamps = `ND`.
75	- **Q5 norm-in-force at t** → `ND` for **every** channel: no channel's content is read, and existence never decides this. (`NO_BY_TYPE` removed.)
76	- **Q6 completeness** → `ND[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]`. **Q6 has a single outcome by design**: the check is existence-only over the tip set, so completeness vs the host can never be shown.
77	- **Q7 independence** → see §3. Reachable: `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`, `IND[…]`, `NOT_INDEPENDENT[…]`, `SELF_ATTESTED[…]`, `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`, `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
78	- **Q8 reproducible** → `YES_LOCAL` (content-addressed, rerunnable on the same tip set) | `NO_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`, unversioned) | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
79	
80	## 3. Independence rule (count overlap only)
81	
82	All sets use the **author** e-mail `%ae` only (never `%ce`), lower-cased, over non-merge commits
83	reachable from the one tip set. Every W, E and N_c `git log` call uses `--full-history` (NB-1), so
84	no history simplification prunes commits. Identities never leave a private temp dir; only counts do.
85	
86	- **W_c** = authors of commits touching candidate c's own paths.
87	- **E** (executors) = authors of commits touching the **CODE / TEST roots of Protocol A r1**:
88	  `app/ routes/ database/ resources/ config/ bootstrap/ lang/ public/ tests/`. Root pathspecs are
89	  used, so historic, renamed and deleted paths under those roots count. **Excluded** (as
90	  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob
91	  translation of the classifier, not the tip path names) and `docs/knowledgeos/**`. Doc and
92	  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,
93	  `scripts/`, `storage/`, READMEs) are **not** executor paths.
94	- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).
95	- **N_c** = authors of commits touching the norm-register paths **minus c's own paths**. N is
96	  never derived from the candidate's own paths. For `K-STATUS` (disjoint from `K-NORMREG` by
97	  construction) N_c = all `K-NORMREG` paths; for `K-NORMREG` N_c's path set is empty.
98	- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).
99	
100	Mapping, applied in this order:
101	1. `K-NORMREG` → `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=…]`. This is a **definitional outcome,
102	   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
103	   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
104	   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
105	   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
106	2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
107	3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
108	   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
109	4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
110	5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`
111	   (an **observed** cross-role authorship).
112	6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
113	   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author
114	   identity is observed; it does not show who controls the channel on the host).
115	
116	**Channels that can reach a positive Q7 (NB-10):** only `K-STATUS` and `K-DEPLOY` (the observable
117	channels, rules 4–6), and only when at least one `K-NORMREG` path exists outside their own paths.
118	`K-NORMREG` is always `SELF_ATTESTED`; `K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`, `K-SIG` and `K-LOCALHOOK` are
119	always `IND`. The positive therefore rests on two channel types.
120	
121	**Disclosed limits of §3:** identity aliases (one person, several e-mails) are **not** resolved, so
122	overlaps may be undercounted and the positive is qualified accordingly; a rename commit spanning a
123	code root and a channel path is still counted in E (and in W_c).
124	
125	## 4. Completeness rule
126	
127	**Checkable locally:** existence of the paths/hooks above in the tip set; per-channel commit count,
128	writer **count** and signature **presence**; writer-overlap counts. **Not checkable locally
129	(declared):** branch-protection enforcement, PR approvals, server audit logs, CI run history, org
130	membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
131	are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule
132	or record *says*) is `ND` because content is not read.
133	
134	## 5. Output (written by `scope_b.sh` into an empty `$OUT` outside the repo)
135	
136	- `60_channel_metrics.tsv` — per channel (`K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY`): `channel, paths, commits, writers, overlap_exec, overlap_norm, norm_paths_c, norm_writers_c` (counts only).
137	- `61_path_ids.tsv` — `16-hex-id → channel` (no path strings leave the repo).
138	- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
139	- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
140	- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
141	- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
142	  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
143	  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;
144	  3. `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED` — else ≥1 Q7 = `NOT_INDEPENDENT…` (observed overlap only);
145	  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local
146	     candidates are self-attested records (definitional, §3 rule 1); **no** independence outcome was
147	     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in
148	     `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED`;
149	  5. `LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED` — else (all local rows `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`).
150	
151	  The headline covers local channels only; host channels stay `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`. Also:
152	  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
153	- `00_script.sha256`, `00_env.tsv` (incl. `repo_local_config=READABLE`), `00_errors.tsv`, and `SHA256SUMS` over every emitted file.
154	
155	**Guarantees:** read-only; `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC`; config isolation (N4, NB-2): system/global config off,
156	`GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` unset,
157	`GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (neutralizes `.git/info/grafts`), and every git call gets `-c log.follow=false
158	-c diff.renames=false -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`
159	(plus `core.quotepath=off`, `log.mailmap=false`, `color.ui=never`); **the repo-local config stays
160	readable** (declared). Pathspec and trace isolation (NB-11): `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS`,
161	`GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS` and every `GIT_TRACE*` /
162	`GIT_TRACE2*` variable are unset. The trace variables are unset by name (`GIT_TRACE`, `GIT_TRACE2`,
163	`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, `GIT_TRACE2_PERF`, `GIT_TRACE_PACKET`, `GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE`, `GIT_TRACE_SETUP`,
164	`GIT_TRACE_CURL`, `GIT_TRACE_PACK_ACCESS`) and also by prefix, so any other `GIT_TRACE…` variable is
165	removed too. No `set -e` (explicit exits 0/1/2/3); own absolute path resolved+hashed
166	**before** the one `cd`; refuses any `$OUT` inside the work tree or `.git`; emits **counts only** —
167	no names, emails, ref names, URLs, owners or path strings. A final `identity_guard` greps `$OUT` for
168	`@`/signature markers and fails **closed**: a hit → `FAIL`, any grep error (rc ≥ 2) → `FAIL(grep_rc)`,
169	both exit 1. The **only** content read beyond existence/size/counts is commit/tag object headers for
170	**signature presence** (Q1/Q2/Q7 for `K-SIG` strictly require it); no file blob is read.
171	
172	## 6. Disclosed limitations (not fixed)
173	
174	- **N7:** `cat-file` errors in the signature loops are not checked (failures count as unsigned); tags are counted per ref, not per object; x509 `SIGNED MESSAGE` tag signatures are missed.
175	- **N8:** in a linked worktree, OUT is checked against the per-worktree gitdir only, not `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.
176	- **N10:** path IDs are unsalted SHA-256 prefixes, so predictable paths can be reversed by dictionary (no identity leak).
177	- **N11:** `$TMP` holds plaintext e-mails (removed on EXIT, not on SIGKILL); `mkdir -p` may create missing parents of OUT.
178	- **N13:** remaining protocol/script mismatches: Q4 omits the content-timestamp qualifier in the output; K-SIG carries no overlap counts; K-LOCALHOOK Q4 = `NONE`; Q8 shows reproducibility, not independent verification; script length.
179	- **N15:** only top-level `docs/knowledgeos/` is excluded as self-contamination; whether `.claude/` / `claude/` hold programme artefacts is not checked.
180	- **NB-4:** READMEs and other markdown *inside* the code roots (e.g. `tests/README.md`) still count as executor work in E.
181	- **NB-5:** under `pipefail`, a commit object larger than the pipe buffer can make `cat-file | awk` fail on SIGPIPE, so a signed commit counts as unsigned (N7 family).
182	- **NB-6:** on an identity-guard `FAIL` the files stay in OUT; only the exit code and the `FAIL` line signal it, so the consumer must honour the exit code.
183	- **NB-7:** in a linked worktree, K-LOCALHOOK checks the per-worktree `$GD/hooks`, not the common dir's hooks (N8 family).
184	- **NB-8:** no cap on per-path `git log` passes or per-commit `cat-file` spawns; a large K-DEPLOY match multiplies the runtime (performance, not safety).
185	- **NB-9:** one sweeping commit (repo-wide reformat/move) puts its author into W_c, N_c and E at once; that overlap is observed, not forced, but it can dominate the counts.
186	- **NB-12:** the token vocabularies also catch data files that are not registers or status records (e.g. `config/decisions.yml` → K-NORMREG, labelled `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register]` by definition; `lang/*/status.json` → K-STATUS), and the r3 infix boundary (BLK-2) widens this imprecision (e.g. `http_status.json`, `x-norm.md`, `.env`, `pre-release.md`).

- the trailing boundary is one of: the extension dot of the basename (→ `.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside the
  basename (→ `[._-]*.$x`); `/` (→ `/**/*.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside a directory segment (→ `[._-]*/**/*.$x`).

For doc tokens, the path-end case `$` cannot occur: the path must end in `.$x`, and no token is a doc
extension. For K-DEPLOY, the path-end case is the bare `$t` form. The construction relies on these git
wildmatch semantics: `*` does not cross `/`; `**/` and `/**/` match zero or more directories; `icase`
is ASCII case folding, like awk `tolower` under `LC_ALL=C`. **No residual mismatch is known at the
pattern level.** The equivalence is argued, not executed. By design (§3), the globs are applied to
historic paths and the regex to tip paths.

**Host-side channels — `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`** (host not authorized): `K-HOST-AUDIT`
(server audit logs), `K-HOST-BRANCHPROT` (branch-protection *enforcement*), `K-HOST-PR-APPROVALS`
(PR approvals), `K-CI-RUNS` (CI run history), `K-HOST-MEMBERS` (org/team membership).

**The one tip set (B1, N5, N12).** Every history query (paths, W, commit counts, E, N_c, K-SIG)
runs over **one** tip file via `git log --stdin` / `git rev-list --stdin`. Tips = refs under
`refs/heads/**`, `refs/remotes/**`, `refs/tags/**` only (`refs/stash`, `refs/notes/**` excluded);
tags are peeled (`^{commit}`), and **only commit-type tips** are kept. The result does not depend
on the checked-out HEAD. Paths are read with `ls-tree -r -z` (N9).

## 2. Deterministic answer rules

Scope = the **tip set only**; completeness vs the host is never shown. `ND` =
`NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK`, `IND` = `INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE`. If a path channel
has **0** paths in the tip trees → Q1 = `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` (it may still exist in history
behind the tips) and Q2..Q8 = `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`; same label for `K-SIG` when no signature is
present in commits reachable from the tips or in tag objects at the tips; `K-LOCALHOOK` uses
`NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY`. Host rows are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` for all eight.

- **Q1 exists** → `YES_IN_CAPTURE` | `YES_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`) | `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` | `NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY` | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
- **Q2 records** → by **type** only: `CONFIG_RULE` (K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-LOCALHOOK), `NORM_REGISTER_RECORD` (K-NORMREG), `STATUS_RECORD` (K-STATUS), `STATE_RECORD_BY_TYPE` (K-DEPLOY), `IDENTITY_ATTESTATION` (K-SIG); content not read.
- **Q3 controls** → `CONTROLLED_BY_WRITERS[n=…]` (count only) | for `K-SIG` `ND(keyring not consulted)` | `LOCAL_MACHINE` (`K-LOCALHOOK`).
- **Q4 timestamps independent** → `NO_CLIENT_SET` (git recording times are client-generated; a self-attested timestamp is **not** independence). Content timestamps = `ND`.
- **Q5 norm-in-force at t** → `ND` for **every** channel: no channel's content is read, and existence never decides this. (`NO_BY_TYPE` removed.)
- **Q6 completeness** → `ND[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]`. **Q6 has a single outcome by design**: the check is existence-only over the tip set, so completeness vs the host can never be shown.
- **Q7 independence** → see §3. Reachable: `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`, `IND[…]`, `NOT_INDEPENDENT[…]`, `SELF_ATTESTED[…]`, `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`, `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
- **Q8 reproducible** → `YES_LOCAL` (content-addressed, rerunnable on the same tip set) | `NO_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`, unversioned) | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.

## 3. Independence rule (count overlap only)

All sets use the **author** e-mail `%ae` only (never `%ce`), lower-cased, over non-merge commits
reachable from the one tip set. Every W, E and N_c `git log` call uses `--full-history` (NB-1), so
no history simplification prunes commits. Identities never leave a private temp dir; only counts do.

- **W_c** = authors of commits touching candidate c's own paths.
- **E** (executors) = authors of commits touching the **CODE / TEST roots of Protocol A r1**:
  `app/ routes/ database/ resources/ config/ bootstrap/ lang/ public/ tests/`. Root pathspecs are
  used, so historic, renamed and deleted paths under those roots count. **Excluded** (as
  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob
  translation of the classifier, not the tip path names) and `docs/knowledgeos/**`. Doc and
  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,
  `scripts/`, `storage/`, READMEs) are **not** executor paths.
- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).
- **N_c** = authors of commits touching the norm-register paths **minus c's own paths**. N is
  never derived from the candidate's own paths. For `K-STATUS` (disjoint from `K-NORMREG` by
  construction) N_c = all `K-NORMREG` paths; for `K-NORMREG` N_c's path set is empty.
- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).

Mapping, applied in this order:
1. `K-NORMREG` → `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=…]`. This is a **definitional outcome,
   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`
   (an **observed** cross-role authorship).
6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author
   identity is observed; it does not show who controls the channel on the host).

**Channels that can reach a positive Q7 (NB-10):** only `K-STATUS` and `K-DEPLOY` (the observable
channels, rules 4–6), and only when at least one `K-NORMREG` path exists outside their own paths.
`K-NORMREG` is always `SELF_ATTESTED`; `K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`, `K-SIG` and `K-LOCALHOOK` are
always `IND`. The positive therefore rests on two channel types.

**Disclosed limits of §3:** identity aliases (one person, several e-mails) are **not** resolved, so
overlaps may be undercounted and the positive is qualified accordingly; a rename commit spanning a
code root and a channel path is still counted in E (and in W_c).

## 4. Completeness rule

**Checkable locally:** existence of the paths/hooks above in the tip set; per-channel commit count,
writer **count** and signature **presence**; writer-overlap counts. **Not checkable locally
(declared):** branch-protection enforcement, PR approvals, server audit logs, CI run history, org
membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule
or record *says*) is `ND` because content is not read.

## 5. Output (written by `scope_b.sh` into an empty `$OUT` outside the repo)

- `60_channel_metrics.tsv` — per channel (`K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY`): `channel, paths, commits, writers, overlap_exec, overlap_norm, norm_paths_c, norm_writers_c` (counts only).
- `61_path_ids.tsv` — `16-hex-id → channel` (no path strings leave the repo).
- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;
  3. `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED` — else ≥1 Q7 = `NOT_INDEPENDENT…` (observed overlap only);
  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local
     candidates are self-attested records (definitional, §3 rule 1); **no** independence outcome was
     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in
     `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED`;
  5. `LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED` — else (all local rows `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`).

  The headline covers local channels only; host channels stay `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`. Also:
  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
- `00_script.sha256`, `00_env.tsv` (incl. `repo_local_config=READABLE`), `00_errors.tsv`, and `SHA256SUMS` over every emitted file.

**Guarantees:** read-only; `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC`; config isolation (N4, NB-2): system/global config off,
`GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` unset,
`GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (neutralizes `.git/info/grafts`), and every git call gets `-c log.follow=false
-c diff.renames=false -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`
(plus `core.quotepath=off`, `log.mailmap=false`, `color.ui=never`); **the repo-local config stays
readable** (declared). Pathspec and trace isolation (NB-11): `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS`,
`GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS` and every `GIT_TRACE*` /
`GIT_TRACE2*` variable are unset. The trace variables are unset by name (`GIT_TRACE`, `GIT_TRACE2`,
`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, `GIT_TRACE2_PERF`, `GIT_TRACE_PACKET`, `GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE`, `GIT_TRACE_SETUP`,
`GIT_TRACE_CURL`, `GIT_TRACE_PACK_ACCESS`) and also by prefix, so any other `GIT_TRACE…` variable is
removed too. No `set -e` (explicit exits 0/1/2/3); own absolute path resolved+hashed
**before** the one `cd`; refuses any `$OUT` inside the work tree or `.git`; emits **counts only** —
no names, emails, ref names, URLs, owners or path strings. A final `identity_guard` greps `$OUT` for
`@`/signature markers and fails **closed**: a hit → `FAIL`, any grep error (rc ≥ 2) → `FAIL(grep_rc)`,
both exit 1. The **only** content read beyond existence/size/counts is commit/tag object headers for
**signature presence** (Q1/Q2/Q7 for `K-SIG` strictly require it); no file blob is read.

## 6. Disclosed limitations (not fixed)

- **N7:** `cat-file` errors in the signature loops are not checked (failures count as unsigned); tags are counted per ref, not per object; x509 `SIGNED MESSAGE` tag signatures are missed.
- **N8:** in a linked worktree, OUT is checked against the per-worktree gitdir only, not `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.
- **N10:** path IDs are unsalted SHA-256 prefixes, so predictable paths can be reversed by dictionary (no identity leak).
- **N11:** `$TMP` holds plaintext e-mails (removed on EXIT, not on SIGKILL); `mkdir -p` may create missing parents of OUT.
- **N13:** remaining protocol/script mismatches: Q4 omits the content-timestamp qualifier in the output; K-SIG carries no overlap counts; K-LOCALHOOK Q4 = `NONE`; Q8 shows reproducibility, not independent verification; script length.
- **N15:** only top-level `docs/knowledgeos/` is excluded as self-contamination; whether `.claude/` / `claude/` hold programme artefacts is not checked.
- **NB-4:** READMEs and other markdown *inside* the code roots (e.g. `tests/README.md`) still count as executor work in E.
- **NB-5:** under `pipefail`, a commit object larger than the pipe buffer can make `cat-file | awk` fail on SIGPIPE, so a signed commit counts as unsigned (N7 family).
- **NB-6:** on an identity-guard `FAIL` the files stay in OUT; only the exit code and the `FAIL` line signal it, so the consumer must honour the exit code.
- **NB-7:** in a linked worktree, K-LOCALHOOK checks the per-worktree `$GD/hooks`, not the common dir's hooks (N8 family).
- **NB-8:** no cap on per-path `git log` passes or per-commit `cat-file` spawns; a large K-DEPLOY match multiplies the runtime (performance, not safety).
- **NB-9:** one sweeping commit (repo-wide reformat/move) puts its author into W_c, N_c and E at once; that overlap is observed, not forced, but it can dominate the counts.
- **NB-12:** the token vocabularies also catch data files that are not registers or status records (e.g. `config/decisions.yml` → K-NORMREG, labelled `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register]` by definition; `lang/*/status.json` → K-STATUS), and the r3 infix boundary (BLK-2) widens this imprecision (e.g. `http_status.json`, `x-norm.md`, `.env`, `pre-release.md`).

2	# scope_b.sh (r3) -- Protocol B scoping. Read-only; existence/metadata only. No network, no host access.
3	# Emits COUNTS ONLY: no names, emails, ref names, URLs or path strings leave TMP; paths -> 16-hex ids.
4	# The ONLY content read beyond existence/counts is commit/tag object headers for signature PRESENCE
5	# (Q1/Q2/Q7 for K-SIG strictly require it); no file blob is ever read.
6	# Usage (from anywhere inside the working clone):  OUT=/abs/empty/dir bash scope_b.sh
7	# Exit: 0 ok | 1 ok-with-unexpected-codes or identity-guard fail | 2 refused | 3 capture invalid
8	set -u -o pipefail
9	export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC GIT_PAGER=cat PAGER=cat GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
10	  GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null  # NB-2: neutralizes .git/info/grafts
11	unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_NAMESPACE GIT_COMMON_DIR \

16	die() { printf 'scope_b: %s\n' "$2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
17

19	SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; case "$SELF" in /*) ;; *) SELF="$PWD/$SELF" ;; esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scope_b.sh (r3) -- Protocol B scoping. Read-only; existence/metadata only. No network, no host access.
# Emits COUNTS ONLY: no names, emails, ref names, URLs or path strings leave TMP; paths -> 16-hex ids.
# The ONLY content read beyond existence/counts is commit/tag object headers for signature PRESENCE
# (Q1/Q2/Q7 for K-SIG strictly require it); no file blob is ever read.
# Usage (from anywhere inside the working clone):  OUT=/abs/empty/dir bash scope_b.sh
# Exit: 0 ok | 1 ok-with-unexpected-codes or identity-guard fail | 2 refused | 3 capture invalid
set -u -o pipefail
export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC GIT_PAGER=cat PAGER=cat GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
  GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null  # NB-2: neutralizes .git/info/grafts
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_NAMESPACE GIT_COMMON_DIR \
  GIT_CONFIG GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS GIT_CONFIG_COUNT   # N4/NB-2: no injected config; repo-local config stays readable (declared)
unset GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS GIT_TRACE GIT_TRACE2 GIT_TRACE2_EVENT GIT_TRACE2_PERF \
  GIT_TRACE_PACKET GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE GIT_TRACE_SETUP GIT_TRACE_CURL GIT_TRACE_PACK_ACCESS   # NB-11: pathspec magic + trace output
for v in $(compgen -v GIT_TRACE); do unset "$v"; done   # NB-11: every remaining GIT_TRACE* / GIT_TRACE2* variable
die() { printf 'scope_b: %s\n' "$2" >&2; exit "$1"; }

# ---- resolve OWN absolute path and hash it BEFORE any cd (corrects earlier relative-BASH_SOURCE defect) ----
SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; case "$SELF" in /*) ;; *) SELF="$PWD/$SELF" ;; esac
SELF="$(realpath -- "$SELF")" || die 2 "cannot resolve own path"
SELFSHA="$(sha256sum < "$SELF" | cut -d' ' -f1)" || die 2 "cannot hash self"
# N4: these overrides are passed to EVERY git call
git() { command git -c core.quotepath=off -c log.mailmap=false -c color.ui=never -c log.follow=false -c diff.renames=false \
  -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false "$@"; }

# ---- preconditions (exit 2) ----
OUT="${OUT:-}"; [ -n "$OUT" ] || die 2 "OUT not set"

GD="$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)" || die 2 "no git dir"

TOPR="$(realpath -- "$TOP")"; GDR="$(realpath -- "$GD")"
for d in "$TOPR" "$GDR"; do case "$OUT/" in "$d"/*) die 2 "OUT must be outside the work tree and .git" ;; esac; done
if [ -e "$OUT" ]; then { [ -d "$OUT" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A -- "$OUT")" ]; } || die 2 "OUT must be an empty directory"; fi
TMP="$(mktemp -d)" || die 2 "mktemp failed"; TMP="$(realpath -- "$TMP")"
case "$TMP/" in "$TOPR"/*|"$GDR"/*|"$OUT"/*) rm -rf -- "$TMP"; die 2 "TMPDIR must be outside the repo and OUT" ;; esac
trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMP"' EXIT
mkdir -p -- "$OUT" || die 2 "cannot create OUT"
cd -- "$TOP" || die 2 "cannot cd to the toplevel"   # the one and only cd; self already resolved+hashed above

ERR="$OUT/00_errors.tsv"; : > "$ERR"; : > "$TMP/e"
ok() { local l="$1" rc="$2" a; shift 2; for a in "$@"; do [ "$rc" = "$a" ] && return 0; done; printf '%s\t%s\n' "$l" "$rc" >> "$ERR"; return 1; }

printf 'git_version\t%s\nrepo_local_config\tREADABLE(not isolated; declared)\n' "$(git --version)" > "$OUT/00_env.tsv"
ND=NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK; IND=INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE
finish() { ( cd -- "$OUT" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS -print | sort | xargs -r -d '\n' sha256sum ) > "$OUT/SHA256SUMS"; exit "$1"; }

# ---- capture validity + THE ONE tip set (B1/N5/N12) -> tracked path universe at tips ----
SH="$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository 2>/dev/null)"; ok env.shallow $? 0
PC="$(git config --get extensions.partialClone)"; ok cfg.partialClone $? 0 1
if [ "$SH" != false ] || [ -n "$PC" ]; then printf 'overall\tCAPTURE_INVALID\n' > "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"; finish 3; fi
# tip set = refs/heads/**, refs/remotes/**, refs/tags/** only (never refs/stash, refs/notes/**); tags peeled; commit-type only
git for-each-ref --format='%(objectname) %(objecttype)' refs/heads refs/remotes refs/tags > "$TMP/refs" 2>>"$TMP/e"; ok refs $? 0
: > "$TMP/t0"
while read -r o ty; do case "$ty" in commit) printf '%s\n' "$o" >> "$TMP/t0" ;;
  tag) git rev-parse --verify -q "$o^{commit}" < /dev/null >> "$TMP/t0" 2>>"$TMP/e"; ok peel $? 0 1 ;; esac; done < "$TMP/refs"
sort -u "$TMP/t0" > "$TMP/tips"
[ -s "$TMP/tips" ] || { printf 'overall\tCAPTURE_INVALID\n' > "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"; finish 3; }
: > "$TMP/paths"   # N9: read with -z; an embedded newline is carried as \001 and restored before any pathspec/hash use
while IFS= read -r t; do git ls-tree -r -z --name-only --full-tree "$t" < /dev/null 2>>"$TMP/e" | tr '\n\0' '\001\n' >> "$TMP/paths"
  ok lstree "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" 0; done < "$TMP/tips"
sort -u "$TMP/paths" > "$TMP/pu"; mv "$TMP/pu" "$TMP/paths"

# ---- classify candidate channels (bounded vocabulary; docs/knowledgeos excluded) ----
# BLK-1/NB-3: K-NORMREG (register regex, trailing token boundary) and K-STATUS (the remaining status records) are disjoint
# BLK-2: leading token boundary (^|[/._-]) -- a token may start a segment or follow . _ - inside a name (K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY)
awk -F'\t' '
{ p=$0; q=tolower(p); b=q; sub(/.*\//,"",b)
  if (q ~ /^docs\/knowledgeos\//) next
  if (q ~ /^[.]github\/workflows\// || q==".gitlab-ci.yml" || b=="jenkinsfile" || q ~ /^[.]circleci\// || q=="azure-pipelines.yml" || q==".drone.yml" || q=="bitbucket-pipelines.yml" || q ~ /^[.]woodpecker/) print "K-CI\t" p
  if (q ~ /^[.]githooks\// || q ~ /^[.]husky\// || q==".pre-commit-config.yaml" || b=="lefthook.yml" || b==".lefthook.yml") print "K-HOOK\t" p
  if (b=="codeowners") print "K-CODEOWNERS\t" p
  e=""; if (b ~ /[.][^.]+$/){e=b; sub(/.*[.]/,"",e)}
  docx=(e=="md"||e=="markdown"||e=="txt"||e=="rst"||e=="json"||e=="yaml"||e=="yml"||e=="toml"||e=="csv"||e=="tsv")
  if (docx && q ~ /(^|[/._-])(rulings?|register|registry|decisions?|norm|inforce|authoriz(ation|ations)?)([._/-]|$)/) print "K-NORMREG\t" p
  else if (docx && q ~ /(^|[/._-])(program_status|status|rulings?|register|registry|decisions?|adoptions?|approvals?|signoffs?|progress|inforce|norm)([._/-]|$)/) print "K-STATUS\t" p
  if (q ~ /(^|[/._-])(deploy|deployment|release|environment|env|infra|terraform)([._/-]|$)/ || e=="tfstate") print "K-DEPLOY\t" p }' \
  "$TMP/paths" | sort -u > "$TMP/cand"

# ---- B3/B4: executor set E = AUTHOR e-mails (%ae only) of non-merge commits touching the Protocol-A r1 CODE/TEST
# ROOTS over the full history of the tip set (NB-1: --full-history); every candidate-channel GLOB pattern and docs/knowledgeos/** excluded.
# BLK-2: per token, segment-start forms (**/$t...) and infix forms (**/*[._-]$t...) -- equivalent to the classifier regex by construction (§1)
ROOTS=( app routes database resources config bootstrap lang public tests )
CHG=( '.github/workflows/**' '.gitlab-ci.yml' '**/jenkinsfile' '.circleci/**' 'azure-pipelines.yml' '.drone.yml' 'bitbucket-pipelines.yml'
  '.woodpecker*' '.woodpecker*/**' '.githooks/**' '.husky/**' '.pre-commit-config.yaml' '**/lefthook.yml' '**/.lefthook.yml' '**/codeowners' '**/*.tfstate' )
for t in program_status status ruling rulings register registry decision decisions adoption adoptions approval approvals signoff signoffs progress inforce norm \
  authoriz authorization authorizations; do
  for x in md markdown txt rst json yaml yml toml csv tsv; do CHG+=( "**/$t.$x" "**/$t[._-]*.$x" "**/$t/**/*.$x" "**/$t[._-]*/**/*.$x" \
    "**/*[._-]$t.$x" "**/*[._-]$t[._-]*.$x" "**/*[._-]$t/**/*.$x" "**/*[._-]$t[._-]*/**/*.$x" ); done; done
for t in deploy deployment release environment env infra terraform; do CHG+=( "**/$t" "**/$t/**" "**/$t[._-]*" "**/$t[._-]*/**" \
  "**/*[._-]$t" "**/*[._-]$t/**" "**/*[._-]$t[._-]*" "**/*[._-]$t[._-]*/**" ); done
PS=( ); for r in "${ROOTS[@]}"; do PS+=( ":(literal)$r" ); done
PS+=( ':(exclude,glob,icase)docs/knowledgeos/**' ); for g in "${CHG[@]}"; do PS+=( ":(exclude,glob,icase)$g" ); done
git log --stdin --no-merges --full-history --format='%ae' -- "${PS[@]}" < "$TMP/tips" 2>>"$TMP/e" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | awk 'NF' | sort -u > "$TMP/E"
ok writers.exec "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" 0; nE=$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/E")
# B2/BLK-1: norm-register paths = the K-NORMREG paths; N_c = their authors MINUS candidate c's own paths
awk -v c="K-NORMREG" 'index($0, c "\t")==1{print substr($0, length(c)+2)}' "$TMP/cand" | sort -u > "$TMP/npaths"

# ---- per-channel metrics (counts only; W, commits, N_c all via --stdin over the one tip set) + path-id map ----
: > "$OUT/61_path_ids.tsv"; : > "$OUT/60_channel_metrics.tsv"
for ch in K-CI K-HOOK K-CODEOWNERS K-NORMREG K-STATUS K-DEPLOY; do
  awk -v c="$ch" 'index($0, c "\t")==1{print substr($0, length(c)+2)}' "$TMP/cand" | sort -u > "$TMP/cp"
  np=$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/cp"); : > "$TMP/W"; nc=0
  while IFS= read -r p; do pr="${p//$'\001'/$'\n'}"
    id="$(printf '%s' "$pr" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"; printf '%s\t%s\n' "$id" "$ch" >> "$OUT/61_path_ids.tsv"
    git log --stdin --no-merges --full-history --format='%ae' -- ":(literal)$pr" < "$TMP/tips" > "$TMP/w1" 2>>"$TMP/e"; ok "w.$id" $? 0
    nc=$((nc + $(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/w1"))); cat "$TMP/w1" >> "$TMP/W"
  done < "$TMP/cp"
  tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' < "$TMP/W" | awk 'NF' | sort -u > "$TMP/Wu"
  comm -23 "$TMP/npaths" "$TMP/cp" > "$TMP/ncp"; nnp=$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/ncp"); : > "$TMP/Nc"
  if [ -s "$TMP/ncp" ]; then NPS=( ); while IFS= read -r p; do NPS+=( ":(literal)${p//$'\001'/$'\n'}" ); done < "$TMP/ncp"
    git log --stdin --no-merges --full-history --format='%ae' -- "${NPS[@]}" < "$TMP/tips" 2>>"$TMP/e" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | awk 'NF' | sort -u > "$TMP/Nc"
    ok "writers.norm.$ch" "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" 0; fi
  nw=$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/Wu"); nn=$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/Nc")
  oe=$(comm -12 "$TMP/Wu" "$TMP/E" | awk 'END{print NR}'); on=$(comm -12 "$TMP/Wu" "$TMP/Nc" | awk 'END{print NR}')
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$ch" "$np" "$nc" "$nw" "$oe" "$on" "$nnp" "$nn" >> "$OUT/60_channel_metrics.tsv"
done

# ---- K-SIG: signature PRESENCE only (justified object-header read; keyring not consulted) ----
git rev-list --stdin < "$TMP/tips" 2>>"$TMP/e" | sort -u > "$TMP/allc"; ok revlist "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" 0
nS=0; while IFS= read -r c; do
  git cat-file commit "$c" < /dev/null 2>>"$TMP/e" | awk '/^$/{exit} /^gpgsig/{s=1} END{exit (s?0:1)}' && nS=$((nS+1)); done < "$TMP/allc"
nTS=0; while IFS= read -r line; do set -- $line; [ "${2:-}" = tag ] || continue
  git cat-file tag "$1" < /dev/null 2>>"$TMP/e" | grep -qE '^-----BEGIN (PGP|SSH) SIGNATURE-----$' && nTS=$((nTS+1)); done < "$TMP/refs"
printf 'commits_total\t%s\ncommits_signed\t%s\ntags_signed\t%s\n' "$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/allc")" "$nS" "$nTS" > "$OUT/58_signatures.tsv"

# ---- K-LOCALHOOK: local .git/hooks presence (LOCAL_ONLY, unversioned) ----
HOOKS="applypatch-msg commit-msg post-checkout post-commit post-merge post-receive post-update pre-applypatch pre-commit pre-merge-commit pre-push pre-rebase pre-receive prepare-commit-msg update"
nh=0; for hk in $HOOKS; do [ -e "$GD/hooks/$hk" ] && nh=$((nh+1)); done
hp=unset; git config --get core.hooksPath > /dev/null 2>&1 && hp=set
printf 'standard_hooks_present\t%s\ncore_hooksPath\t%s\n' "$nh" "$hp" > "$OUT/56_local_hooks.tsv"

# ---- answers Q1..Q8 (deterministic; every outcome reachable; never a forced negative) ----
NA7='NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)\tNOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)'
{
printf '#channel\tQ1_exists\tQ2_records\tQ3_controls\tQ4_ts_independent\tQ5_norm_at_t\tQ6_complete\tQ7_independent\tQ8_reproducible\n'
awk -F'\t' -v ND="$ND" -v IND="$IND" -v nE="$nE" 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"; na="NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)"}
{ ch=$1; np=$2+0; nw=$4+0; oe=$5+0; on=$6+0; nnp=$7+0; nn=$8+0
  if (np==0){ print ch,"NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS",na,na,na,na,na,na,na; next }
  cfg=(ch=="K-CI"||ch=="K-HOOK"||ch=="K-CODEOWNERS")
  q2=cfg?"CONFIG_RULE(by type; content not read)":(ch=="K-NORMREG"?"NORM_REGISTER_RECORD(by type; content not read)":(ch=="K-STATUS"?"STATUS_RECORD(by type; content not read)":"STATE_RECORD_BY_TYPE(content not read)"))
  ov="overlap_exec=" oe ";overlap_norm=" (nnp>0 ? on : "NA")
  if (ch=="K-NORMREG") q7="SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=" oe "]"   # BLK-1: by declared definition, not an observed negative
  else if (nnp==0) q7=IND "[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;" ov "]"
  else if (cfg) q7=IND "[mechanism_host_enforced_unobservable;" ov "]"
  else if (nw==0 || nn==0 || nE==0) q7=IND "[empty_set;W=" nw ";N_c=" nn ";E=" nE "]"
  else if (on>0) q7="NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm=" on "]"
  else if (oe>0) q7="NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec=" oe "]"
  else q7="INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]"
  print ch,"YES_IN_CAPTURE",q2,"CONTROLLED_BY_WRITERS[n=" nw "]","NO_CLIENT_SET(git recording times are client-generated)",ND,ND "[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]",q7,"YES_LOCAL(content-addressed; rerunnable on same ref set)" }' \
  "$OUT/60_channel_metrics.tsv"
read -r nC nSg nTg < <(awk -F'\t' '{v[$1]=$2} END{print v["commits_total"]+0, v["commits_signed"]+0, v["tags_signed"]+0}' "$OUT/58_signatures.tsv")
if [ "$nSg" -gt 0 ] || [ "$nTg" -gt 0 ]; then
  printf 'K-SIG\tYES_IN_CAPTURE\tIDENTITY_ATTESTATION(presence only; not verified)\t%s(keyring not consulted)\tNO_CLIENT_SET(signer clock)\t%s\t%s[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]\t%s(signatures not verified)\tYES_LOCAL(presence only)\n' "$ND" "$ND" "$ND" "$IND"
else printf "K-SIG\tNOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS\t$NA7\n"; fi
read -r hn hpv < <(awk -F'\t' '{v[$1]=$2} END{print v["standard_hooks_present"]+0, v["core_hooksPath"]}' "$OUT/56_local_hooks.tsv")
if [ "$hn" -gt 0 ] || [ "$hpv" = set ]; then
  printf 'K-LOCALHOOK\tYES_LOCAL_ONLY\tCONFIG_RULE(by type; content not read)\tLOCAL_MACHINE\tNONE\t%s\t%s[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]\t%s(local, unversioned)\tNO_LOCAL_ONLY(not versioned; not reproducible from the ref set)\n' "$ND" "$ND" "$IND"
else printf "K-LOCALHOOK\tNOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY\t$NA7\n"; fi
for hc in K-HOST-AUDIT K-HOST-BRANCHPROT K-HOST-PR-APPROVALS K-CI-RUNS K-HOST-MEMBERS; do
  printf '%s\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\tNOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY\n' "$hc"; done
} > "$OUT/70_answers.tsv"

# ---- overall: headline COMPUTED from the per-channel Q7 values (N2/N14/BLK-1) + fail-closed identity guard (N6) ----
q7n() { awk -F'\t' -v r="$1" 'NR>1 && $8 ~ r {c++} END{print c+0}' "$OUT/70_answers.tsv"; }
nI=$(q7n '^INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL'); nD=$(q7n '^INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE'); nX=$(q7n '^NOT_INDEPENDENT'); nA=$(q7n '^SELF_ATTESTED')
# BLK-1: SELF_ATTESTED has its own bucket (4th); it never counts towards LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED
if [ "$nI" -gt 0 ]; then HL=LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL; elif [ "$nD" -gt 0 ]; then HL=LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE
elif [ "$nX" -gt 0 ]; then HL=LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED; elif [ "$nA" -gt 0 ]; then HL=LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS
else HL=LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED; fi
nNE=$(awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $2 ~ /^NOT_EVIDENCED/{c++} END{print c+0}' "$OUT/70_answers.tsv")
printf 'headline\t%s\ncomplete_vs_host\tNOT_SHOWN\nindependent_at_identity_count_level\t%s\nopen_local_candidates\t%s\nnot_independent_by_overlap\t%s\nself_attested\t%s\nnot_evidenced\t%s\nhost_channels\t5\n' \
  "$HL" "$nI" "$nD" "$nX" "$nA" "$nNE" > "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"
code=0; [ -s "$ERR" ] && code=1
grep -rlE '@|BEGIN (PGP|SSH) SIGNATURE' -- "$OUT" > "$TMP/hit" 2>/dev/null; g=$?
if [ "$g" -eq 1 ]; then printf 'identity_guard\tPASS\n' >> "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"
elif [ "$g" -eq 0 ]; then printf 'identity_guard\tFAIL(%s files)\n' "$(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/hit")" >> "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"; code=1
else printf 'identity_guard\tFAIL(grep_rc=%s)\n' "$g" >> "$OUT/71_overall.tsv"; code=1; fi
finish "$code"

# Output review — Protocol B (r3) execution

**Verdict: PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS.**
- Every answer in `70_answers.tsv` and the headline in `71_overall.tsv` match my hand recomputation from `60`, `58` and `56` under PROTOCOL-B §2, §3 and §5.

  - the K-NORMREG vocabulary probably over-captures (§4.2).
- I did not recompute any hash, because I had no shell in this review.

Sources: PROTOCOL-B.md, scope_b.sh (r3), REVIEW-r3.md, RUN-RECORD.md, SHA256SUMS-RUN-APP, QUESTIONS.md, and the ten files in RUN-ROOT/. I did not execute anything.

This review describes the outputs only. It does not interpret them for any hypothesis (H-D, H-B or any other).

---

## 1. Integrity

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| SHA256SUMS coverage | It lists 9 files: `00_env`, `00_errors`, `00_script.sha256`, `56`, `58`, `60`, `61`, `70`, `71`. Together with `SHA256SUMS` itself, which `finish()` leaves out by design, that is all 10 files §5 specifies, and all 10 are present in RUN-ROOT. Any extra file present at `finish()` would have been hashed, and none was. |
| Hash values | **I did not recompute them** (I had no shell). One value checks out by inspection: `00_errors.tsv` is empty, and its listed hash `e3b0c442…b855` is the SHA-256 of the empty string. |
| Script hash | `00_script.sha256` = `e9e0975b…37a8`, which is the hash RUN-RECORD gives. I did not confirm that the local `scope_b.sh` hashes to this value. |
| Two runs identical | `SHA256SUMS-RUN-APP` and `RUN-ROOT/SHA256SUMS` are line-for-line identical (compared by reading). The `diff -r` IDENTICAL result is RUN-RECORD's claim; I did not re-run it. Apart from SHA256SUMS, the app-run output files were not available to me. |
| Exit codes | RUN-RECORD gives 0 for both runs. This is consistent with the script: code 0 requires an empty `00_errors.tsv` and guard rc 1, and the outputs show both (empty file, `identity_guard PASS`). |
| Errors file | Empty, in agreement with its hash. |
| HEAD record | `9f1bcab5…`, "unchanged before and after", appears **only in RUN-RECORD**. No output file records HEAD, the tip count or the ref-set hash. That is consistent with the protocol (§1: the result does not depend on HEAD). However, Q8 says "rerunnable on same ref set", and no output pins that ref set (see A6). |
| Internal consistency | `61_path_ids.tsv` has 394 rows: 6 K-CI, 3 K-HOOK, 202 K-NORMREG, 153 K-STATUS and 30 K-DEPLOY. These equal the `paths` column of `60`. |

## 2. Conformance (hand recomputation)

Inputs from `60`: `channel, paths, commits, writers, oe, on, nnp, nn`. From `58`, `commits_signed`=23 and `tags_signed`=0. From `56`, hooks=0 and hooksPath=unset.

| Channel | Rule path | Expected Q7 | Observed Q7 | ok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K-CI | np=6>0; not NORMREG; nnp=202>0; cfg → rule 3 | `IND[mechanism_host_enforced_unobservable;overlap_exec=1;overlap_norm=1]` | same | ✔ |
| K-HOOK | np=3; cfg → rule 3 | `IND[mechanism_host_enforced_unobservable;overlap_exec=1;overlap_norm=1]` | same | ✔ |
| K-CODEOWNERS | np=0 | `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)` (Q1 `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS`) | same | ✔ |
| K-NORMREG | rule 1 (definitional) | `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=3]` | same | ✔ |
| K-STATUS | observable; W=3, N_c=3, E≥3 (implied by oe=3); on=3>0 → rule 5 | `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm=3]` | same | ✔ |
| K-DEPLOY | observable; W=3, N_c=3, E≥3; on=3>0 → rule 5 | `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm=3]` | same | ✔ |
| K-SIG | signed=23>0 | `IND(signatures not verified)` | same | ✔ |

- **Q1–Q6 and Q8** match the script's mapping on every row:
  - Q3 `n=1/1/3/3/3`;
  - Q5 = `ND` on every evidenced row;
  - Q6 = the single outcome;
  - Q4 for K-SIG = `NO_CLIENT_SET(signer clock)`.
- **Headline.** The local Q7 values are 0 × INDEPENDENT…, 3 × `IND` (K-CI, K-HOOK, K-SIG), 2 × `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and 1 × `SELF_ATTESTED`. By first match, the headline is `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE`. The observed headline is the same, and so are the counts 0 / 3 / 2 / 1, `not_evidenced`=2 and `host_channels`=5. **headline_ok = true.**

## 3. Identity

- **What the outputs hold:** counts, 16-hex path IDs, protocol labels, `git version 2.55.0`, and the script hash.
- **What they do not hold:** no `@`, no e-mail, no name, no ref name, no URL, no path string and no signature block. **identity_ok = true.**
- **Residual risk:** this is the declared N10. The path IDs are unsalted, so predictable paths can be reversed by dictionary. That exposes paths, not identities.

## 4. Anomalies requiring disclosure

**A1 — Very small identity sets mean the overlap test has almost no statistical power.**
- The counts are |W| ≤ 3 for every channel (1 for K-CI and K-HOOK) and |N_c| = 3. |E| is **not emitted**; it is ≥ 3, inferred from overlap_exec = 3.
- The commit volume is large (4028 commits) compared with these sets. The whole author-e-mail universe may be only about 3 identities, but the outputs do not show its size.
- When |W_c| + |N_c| exceeds the universe size, a zero overlap is impossible under any assignment of identities. Overlap counts of 3/3 then show that the few identities all touched both path sets. They do not discriminate between role arrangements.
- In the other direction, a zero overlap at these sizes would also be fragile.
- Aliases are unresolved, so 3 e-mails may stand for fewer people, or for non-human authors (tools or agents).
- I note this as a property of the test at these counts, not as a reading of the result.

**A2 — K-NORMREG over-capture (NB-12, NB-13 and N15).**
- **Size.** K-NORMREG has 202 tip paths (409 path-commit touches, 3 writers), and K-STATUS has 153.
- **Vocabulary.** The tokens include `decision(s)`, `norm`, `register`, `authoriz*` and `ruling(s)`, with the r3 infix boundary. They can catch:
  - developer data and i18n files;
  - test fixtures;
  - config, including code-root files that are then removed from E.
- **Self-contamination (N15).** Only top-level `docs/knowledgeos/` is excluded. `.claude/` and `claude/` are neither excluded nor checked, so programme-adjacent artefacts there may be counted as "norm register" paths. That would be the same self-contamination the knowledgeos rule exists to prevent.
- **Consequence (NB-13).** All 202 paths make up N_c for K-STATUS and K-DEPLOY. So `overlap_norm=3` may partly be developer authorship labelled with the norm role, and it may partly come from programme artefacts.
- **Not visible in the outputs.** The outputs contain no path strings, so the composition cannot be determined from them.

**A3 — K-SIG: 23 of 4028 commits carry a signature header, and 0 tags are signed.**
- **What was checked.** Only the presence of a header. Signatures were not verified and the keyring was not consulted.
- **Merges are counted.** `rev-list` here does not use `--no-merges`, so merge commits are included. W, E and N_c exclude them.
